text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on about 300-350 W of solar. A 200 W panel does it in about 1.5 days of decent sun.**

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The derate covers heat, panel angle and charging losses. [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) uses 0.75, and [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) uses 0.7.

**For a 1,000 Wh station, from empty to full in one day:**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (cloudy or shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

These come from [Power Runtime's table](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives about 300 W in summer and 700 W or more in a northern winter.

**Common panel sizes:** At 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency, [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) estimates:
- **100 W:** ~315 Wh/day, so about 3 days.
- **200 W:** ~630 Wh/day, so about 1.5 days.
- **400 W:** ~1,260 Wh/day, so under a day.

The same source offers a quick rule: battery Wh ÷ 5 gives the panel wattage that refills it in about a day and a half, so roughly 200 W here.

**Check these before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station accepts only so many watts, and extra panel wattage beyond that adds nothing. Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Going over can damage the charge controller. Wiring panels in series adds their voltages ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** Panels usually come with MC4 plugs, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel ports, so confirm you have the right adapter.
- **Winter and running loads:** Winter sun and powering devices while charging both slow recharging considerably.

If you tell me your station's model, I can check its solar input limits and suggest a compatible panel with a buy link.
